rows.answer: As of 2022-10-13, QQQ is in the panic regime: the Composite Panic Index reads 79.8, well above the 64 buy threshold. That is a very elevated reading — the 92.7nd percentile of the index's history available at that date, i.e. only about 7% of prior observations were higher. The components: VIX at 31.94 and CNN Fear & Greed at 19.37 ("extreme fear", inverted into the composite). QQQ closed at 263.1. The framework treats this as a threshold-based accumulation/exposure-increase environment. The strategy is already at its 100% cap, so the latest observation was a hold with no change; the standard backtest (2021-05-17 to 2022-10-13) shows strategy -21.73% vs. Buy & Hold -16.43%, so Buy & Hold beat the strategy on return and Sharpe. Historical research only, not investment advice.

Over the standard window (2021-05-17 to 2023-12-29, 661 observations) the SMH threshold strategy returned 26.69% versus 55.05% for Buy & Hold, so Buy & Hold beat the strategy on return. Risk metrics favored Buy & Hold too: both had the same max drawdown of -45.3%, while Sharpe was 0.445 vs. 0.668 and Calmar 0.209 vs. 0.403. Average exposure was 74.6%, with the strategy below full exposure 34.2% of the time; reduced exposure cost 106.04 pp of upside and saved 83.87 pp on the downside. The latest reading (2023-12-29) is greed at a Panic Index of 10.42 (percentile 0.6), and the rule holds 0% exposure. This is historical research, not investment advice.

Since the backtest window begins 2021-05-17, SPX panic-regime days (Panic Index > 64, threshold 64) number 111 through 2024-06-28, with the last such day on 2023-03-17. One month (21 trading days) later, the mean return was +2.86% and the median +4.32%, with 73.0% of these overlapping days positive (range -10.32% to +12.92%). At three months (63 trading days), the edge faded: mean +0.47%, median -0.04%, win rate 48.6% (range -13.03% to +12.59%). So the historical tilt was toward a short-term bounce, not a durable three-month gain. Today's regime is neutral — Panic Index 29.02 (percentile 28.7), VIX 12.44, Fear & Greed 44.31 — so no threshold-driven exposure change is indicated, and the rule holds 0% exposure. Historical research, not investment advice.

Yes. The causal (no-look-ahead) panic-reversal detector fired twice for QQQ in the April 2025 selloff: on 2025-04-09, when the Panic Index had reached 72.13 with QQQ at 463.76, and on 2025-04-11, with the Panic Index at 77.56 and QQQ at 452.21. Each date is the session where a reversal was confirmed using only data available up to that date. Since then the index has unwound: as of 2025-05-30 the Panic Index is 27.33 (percentile 31.3) with VIX 18.57 and CNN Fear & Greed 61.91 (greed), putting QQQ in the neutral regime, so the rule holds its 100% exposure. Note this is historical research, not investment advice.

At its June 15, 2022 meeting the FOMC raised the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent and said ongoing increases will likely be appropriate, while continuing to shrink Treasury and agency MBS holdings as laid out in the May balance-sheet plans. In his press conference, Chair Powell called the 75-basis-point move unusually large and said moves of that size should not be common, with a 50 or 75 bp increase most likely next, decided meeting by meeting. Yes — the market is in a panic regime: the SPX Composite Panic Index is 79.13 (92.4th percentile, VIX 31.13, Fear & Greed 16.93). The strategy therefore holds 100% exposure (unchanged, at the cap), reducing 10% only if the index closes below 15.

The most recent statement as of 2023-03-24 is the March 22, 2023 FOMC statement (statement-20230322). It said: "The U.S. banking system is sound and resilient. Recent developments are likely to result in tighter credit conditions for households and businesses and to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation. The extent of these effects is uncertain. The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks." Chair Powell, at that day's press conference, said the system is sound and resilient with strong capital and liquidity, that the Fed, Treasury and FDIC took decisive actions so all depositors' savings and the banking system are safe, and that deposit flows stabilized over the past week. Separately, on your framing: the dashboard shows SPX in a neutral regime (Panic Index 46.84, percentile 55.8), not the panic regime, with 100% exposure held. This is historical research, not investment advice.

On the historical record available as of 2025-04-11, DJI panic-regime days have been a mildly favorable entry backdrop, though with overlap-adjusted caveats. The Panic Index is 77.56 (99.6th percentile; VIX 37.56, Fear & Greed 8.39, extreme fear). Forward returns after prior DJI panic-regime days (Panic Index above 64, since 2021-05-17) were positive on average at every horizon: +1.43% at 5 days (68.3% win rate), +4.21% at 21 days (71.8%), and +4.99% at 63 days (66.7%). But the tails were wide (21-day range −5.69% to +15.42%), and the realtime panic-reversal detector just confirmed a signal today, so the current move is unproven. The strategy holds 100% exposure (no change today, already at the cap), and the backtest's 4.78% return lagged Buy & Hold's 17.14% over the window. This is historical research, not investment advice.

The most recent FOMC decision (Sept 18, 2024) was to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point to 4-3/4 to 5 percent, citing progress on inflation and risks that are roughly in balance; Governor Bowman dissented, preferring a 1/4-point cut. Chair Powell described it as a "recalibration" of policy stance and stressed the Committee is "not on any preset course." For QQQ as of 2024-09-20, the Composite Panic Index reads 27.43 (percentile 25.7), built from VIX 16.15 and CNN Fear & Greed 61.2 (greed), placing the market in the neutral regime between the 64 panic and 15 greed thresholds. With the index neutral, the strategy's signal is to hold, with exposure unchanged at 60% of the 0%-100% band.

For SMH in 2022 the two detectors agree on the broad shape but differ in count and timing: the realtime (causal) detector fired 13 signals (2022-03-03 through 2022-10-17), while scipy's hindsight labels mark 8 peaks (2022-01-26 through 2022-12-12). Realtime signals cluster in panic-heavy clusters, often several per episode (e.g., 10-03, 10-13, 10-17; 05-03/05-13/05-19), and occur at lower Panic Index readings (67.97–81.66) after a 5% retreat from a local max. Scipy peaks sit at higher local maxima (up to 91.94 on 05-09) and include the 02-14 and 12-12 labels (68.22 and 44.70) that the causal rule did not flag. Hindsight dates are not tradable; the realtime list is the one a backtest could use. This is research, not investment advice.

The March 2022 meeting minutes cannot be used: they were released about three weeks after the March 15-16 meeting, so as of 2022-03-25 they were not public yet (the search returns no such document). The published statement from that meeting only says the Committee "expects to begin reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities at a coming meeting" — no caps were announced. On caps, the most recent available minutes (January 2022) only note that participants judged a faster runoff than 2017-19 likely and left timing and pace to upcoming meetings; December 2021 minutes said monthly caps could make runoff measured and predictable. Nothing on specific cap levels. This is historical research, not investment advice.

As of 2024-08-30, the September 2024 FOMC decision had not yet occurred, so I cannot report what the Committee decided — the tools contain no statement, minutes, or press conference for that meeting on or before this date. The latest decision in the document library is the July 31, 2024 statement, which kept the target range at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent (doc_id statement-20240731). Chair Powell said at his July press conference that 'we have made no decisions about future meetings, and that includes the September meeting,' while noting a reduction 'could be on the table as soon as the next meeting in September' if the totality of data supported it (doc_id press_conference-20240731).

rows.answer: Since 2023 the greed regime (<15 on the Panic Index) kept QQQ exposure well below full: the backtest window 2023-01-03 to 2024-12-31 shows 44 greed signal days (last 2024-03-04) and average exposure of only 29.5%, with exposure below 100% on 100% of days. Each greed day trimmed 10%, so the strategy returned 42.19% versus Buy & Hold 95.79%. Upside drag was 167.66pp against a downside cushion of 133.15pp, i.e. the reduced exposure cost more in foregone gains than it saved in losses, though max drawdown was only -4.24% vs -13.56% and Sharpe 2.138 vs 1.973. Averaged over greed days, forward returns were mildly positive (21-day mean 1.52%, 65.9% win rate), so those reductions typically preceded gains. Current exposure is 60% and the signal is hold. This is historical research, not investment advice.
